messages.subject: comparing learning effect on different CAT tests
messages.subject_clean: comparing learning effect on different CAT tests
messages.body_plain:
I have two online ability tests for which I am creating the models using the mirt package.
Both have a relatively large item bank (n>200) relatively few items displayed in a test (n=25) and quite a lot of test results (n>5k) that I gut using adaptive testing - so a large, but sparse response matrix.
Though the models seem to fit well in both cases I presume that there is a significantly larger learning effect (people get better by doing the test - violation of local independence) for one of the tests - is there a way to test this hypothesis?

Many thanks.
Balázs

Hi Phil,

Thank you for all the work you put into the mirt package: it's a life-saver!

I have been working on my dissertation comparing several different IRT models for an instrument.  All of the models converged successfully and without any warnings.  However, when I examine the AIC and DIC values for every model, the values are identical.  My (limited) understanding of these fit measures is that it is very unlikely that they are identical, especially in multiple models.

Below I have pasted the output from calling the object as well as the DIC values, with the AIC and DIC values highlighted.  The same problem occurs when I ran the models as generalized partial credit models as well.  Any light you could shine on this oddity would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Dave Periard
Ph.D Candidate in Industrial/Organizational Psychology and Human Factors
Wright State University

messages.subject_clean: DIC and AIC are equal?
messages.body_plain:

Phil

messages.subject: Re: RMSEA and M*2 STATISTICS
messages.subject_clean: RMSEA and M*2 STATISTICS
messages.body_plain:
On Sat, Apr 9, 2016 at 10:29 AM, Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
>

> On Thu, Apr 7, 2016 at 5:29 AM, Serpil çelikten <sserpil...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear Phil,
> > I have two questions about the model fit statistics.
> >
> > First, what is the critical point to evaluate model fit based on the M*2 statisic for polytomous models? How could I decide whether the model fits or not?
>

> That's difficult to answer, as fit measures are really just descriptives, and 'gold standards' of fit are largely meaningless anyway. Use judgment of fit, and if you can't tell what a good fit is then just report what you actually observe and avoid interpretation all together.

>
> >
> > Second, what is the difference between these statistics RMSEA ,  RMSEA_5 ,  RMSEA_95? Which one should I pick to evaluate my model fit?
>

> The _5 and _95 are the 90% confidence interval bounds for the RMSEA statistic.
>
> Phil

messages.body_plain:
Dear researchers,

First, I would like to thank Phil for making such an amazing programme mirt to do various complex IRT modeling. It is very useful and it is one of the best programmes to conduct the analysis.

When I tried out the mirt programme, I get the following message:

Item re-scored so that all values are within a distance of 1

Also, the programme is running extremely slow.

I briefly check the data and found that the values do not have decimal places. I wonder if this is because in certain items (with Likert scale from 1 to 5), for example, some options have never been chosen? What are the other possible reasons behind this warning?

Thank you,
Chester Kam

messages.body_plain:
Sounds like there is a lot going on in this model. The information matrix not being PD might suggest the model isn't identified, so that could be a large problem, and it looks like you might have a large amount of missing data (in which imputation isn't a good idea anyway). Collapsing responses would certainly help with stability, but even then you may have issues if too many parameters are being estimated. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject_clean: multidimensional grsmIRT in confirmatory style..
messages.body_plain:
That's sort of the problem with all the classical IRT parametrizations, they really don't generalize well to multidimensional models (at least, not intuitively or obviously). This is mainly why I use the slope-intercept form wherever possible in all items. So I think for multidimensional models, you should resort to the grsm itemtype. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Do you have option to fix COV of factors when using multipleGroup
messages.subject_clean: Do you have option to fix COV of factors when using multipleGroup
messages.body_plain:
Are you certain you want to do this? Constraining covariances implies that the variances should be equal as well, which in some models doesn't work because the reference group is set to N(0, Σ), where diag(Σ) = 1 for identification. If your variances will be estimated though (like in Rasch models) then you could probably pass the appropriate constrains to the constraints = list() input (?mirt), after obtaining their location with pars = 'values', to ensure that both the variances and covariances are equal. It's a bit awkward, but I do this generally to deter people from constraining covariances accidently when variances are unequal. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: IIF bimodality and item misfit
messages.subject_clean: IIF bimodality and item misfit
messages.body_plain:
These items are basically step-function items similar to what you would find in latent class models. They generally aren't all that great for latent trait models because all they really tell you is who is above some exact latent trait level. So removing them might make the most sense, otherwise placing prior distributions on them may also help to pull the slopes away from ∞ (they also seem to have some sparse categories according to the intercept terms, which might be part of the problem). Cheers.

Phil
